title: Moose Has Never Been WRONG
premise: In our town a dog barks once for a stranger who means well and twice for one who doesn't, and our dog barked once at my sister's fiance at the gate and twice when I was alone with him at the grill.
twist: The trusted source contradicts itself: there are clues both ways (he knew the dog's name and pocketed Grandma's ring box, but the dog shared its toy with him and the second bark was aimed past him at the open gate), and I ask which bark to trust.
world: Our sunny backyard on a Sunday: a green lawn, a white picket fence with a side gate, a red brick patio, a kettle grill, a picnic table with a gingham cloth, bunting, and the back of our yellow house.
